title: Underived tensor comparison for pullback of modules on ringed topoi
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small relative to the universe of the module sheaves, with sheaves of commutative rings $R,S$, and let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a morphism of topoi, an adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ with $u^{-1}$ preserving finite limits, equipped with a ring map $c:u^{-1}R\to S$. On module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] put $u^*M=S\otimes_{u^{-1}R}u^{-1}M$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For $R$-module sheaves $M,N$ there is a canonical $S$-linear isomorphism $u^*(M\otimes_RN)\xrightarrow{\sim}u^*M\otimes_Su^*N$, natural simultaneously in $M,N$.

proof.text: Put $L=u^{-1}$, $P=u_*$, $A=LR$, $X=LM$, $Y=LN$, and let $H$ be any $S$-module sheaf, also regarded as an $A$-module via $c$. Give $PH$ the $R$-action specified in the module adjunction node. That adjunction followed by the sheaf tensor universal property gives bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_S(u^*(M\otimes_RN),H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(M\otimes_RN,PH)\cong\mathrm{Bilin}_R(M\times N,PH)$, natural in $H$. The hypotheses of the adjunction node are exactly the given geometric morphism and ring map.

Let $\lambda_{V,W}:L(V\times W)\xrightarrow{\sim}LV\times LW$ be the finite-product comparison and $\eta,\varepsilon$ the set adjunction unit and counit. The group/ring lifting node identifies the operations on the inverse images with the images of the operations through these comparisons; the unit and counit respect the group/ring operations. For a sheaf map $b:M\times N\to PH$ define $\beta=\varepsilon_H\circ Lb\circ\lambda_{M,N}^{-1}:X\times Y\to H$. Conversely send $\beta$ to $P\beta\circ\langle\eta_M,\eta_N\rangle$. Naturality of $\eta$ and the two triangle identities show that these are inverse: this is the set adjunction bijection for $M\times N$, with $\eta_{M\times N}$ identified with the pair of units by its projections.

This bijection restricts to bilinear maps. Indeed transpose the first additivity equation $b\circ(+_M\times\mathrm{id}_N)=+_{PH}\circ\langle b\circ(p_1,p_3),b\circ(p_2,p_3)\rangle$, whose domain is $M\times M\times N$. Preservation of this triple product and naturality of the counit turn it into $\beta(x+x\prime,y)=\beta(x,y)+\beta(x\prime,y)$. The equation on $M\times N\times N$ gives second-variable additivity. Zero equations use the terminal-object comparison. For the scalar equation on $R\times M\times N$, transposition sends the $R$-action on $PH$ to the $A$-action on $H$: the former is induced by $R\xrightarrow{\eta_R}PA\xrightarrow{Pc}PS$ and the latter by $c:A\to S$, and $\varepsilon_S\circ L(Pc\circ\eta_R)=c$ by naturality and a triangle identity. Consequently $b(rm,n)=r b(m,n)$ transposes to $\beta(ax,y)=c(a)\beta(x,y)$, and the second-variable equation transposes in the same way. Because transposition is injective, these implications are equivalences. Thus $\mathrm{Bilin}_R(M\times N,PH)\cong\mathrm{Bilin}_A(X\times Y,H)$, naturally in $H,M,N$. This calculation uses only the finite-product comparisons and operations supplied by the cited lifting statement, rather than assuming a module or bilinear version of that statement.

An $A$-bilinear map $\beta:X\times Y\to H$ extends uniquely to an $S$-bilinear map $\widetilde\beta:(S\otimes_AX)\times(S\otimes_AY)\to H$ by $\widetilde\beta(s\otimes x,t\otimes y)=st\beta(x,y)$. The balancing relation in the first factor is respected because $sc(a)t\beta(x,y)=st\beta(ax,y)$; the second uses $stc(a)\beta(x,y)=st\beta(x,ay)$. Additivity follows from that of $\beta$ and distributivity in $S$. For clarity, form the sectionwise presheaves $E(U)=S(U)\otimes_{A(U)}X(U)$ and $F(U)=S(U)\otimes_{A(U)}Y(U)$. The formula defines a restriction-compatible $S$-bilinear presheaf map $E\times F\to H$. Its sheafification gives the asserted bilinear map on $E^\#\times F^\#$: sheafification of sets preserves products, so the universal set-sheafification map extends it uniquely, and sheafifying the addition and scalar equations preserves those equations. The underlying sets of the module sheafification are the set sheafification here: the sheafification notion explicitly permits sets and abelian groups, and the module-sheafification definition gives its unique induced action. Equivalently one may build the abelian sheafification by sheafifying the group-operation diagrams as in the lifting node. Thus by the definition of the sheaf tensor product $E^\#=S\otimes_AX$, $F^\#=S\otimes_AY$. Conversely restrict an $S$-bilinear map along $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, $y\mapsto1\otimes y$. The two operations are inverse by $S$-bilinearity and uniqueness in the tensor universal property. Commutativity of $S$ is used for the product $st$. Applying that property once more identifies these maps with $\operatorname{Hom}_S(u^*M\otimes_Su^*N,H)$.

Let $B=u^*(M\otimes_RN)$ and $T=u^*M\otimes_Su^*N$. Composing the preceding bijections gives $\Phi_H:\operatorname{Hom}_S(B,H)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_S(T,H)$ natural in $H$. Set $a=\Phi_B(\mathrm{id}_B):T\to B$ and $d=\Phi_T^{-1}(\mathrm{id}_T):B\to T$. Naturality gives $\Phi_H(f)=f\circ a$. Hence $d\circ a=\mathrm{id}_T$, and injectivity of $\Phi_B$ applied to $a\circ d$ and $\mathrm{id}_B$ gives $a\circ d=\mathrm{id}_B$. Thus $d$ is the required $S$-linear isomorphism; no stalk or enough-points hypothesis is used.

Each bijection commutes with precomposition in $M,N$: the module adjunction is natural, tensor factorization is unique, set transposition uses natural unit/counit, and the extension formula sends $(s\otimes x,t\otimes y)$ to $st\beta(x,y)$. Therefore for maps $f:M\to M\prime$, $g:N\to N\prime$ both composites of the comparison with $u^*(f\otimes g)$ and with $u^*f\otimes u^*g$ correspond to the same bilinear map. Explicitly the comparison is adjoint to $(m,n)\mapsto(1\otimes\eta_M(m))\otimes(1\otimes\eta_N(n))$, with the set units interpreted before extension of scalars; both routes replace $m,n$ by $f(m),g(n)$. The adjunction and tensor bijections detect equality, proving simultaneous naturality and fixing the canonical normalization.
